issues.body:
scripts/selftest-suite.txt now enrolls `yaml_dependency.py`. `_derive_full_selftest_suite` (scripts/worker-live.sh:1039-1057) independently DISCOVERS which scripts advertise a `--self-test` entrypoint using this ERE at worker-live.sh:1043:

  ^[[:space:]]*[^#].*(add_argument\("--self-test"|"--self-test"[[:space:]]+in[[:space:]]+sys\.argv|sys\.argv\[[^]]+\][[:space:]]*==[[:space:]]*"--self-test")

yaml_dependency.py:88 spells it `if sys.argv[1:] == ["--self-test"]:`. Trace the only candidate alternative: `sys\.argv\[` matches, `[^]]+` matches `1:`, `\]` matches `]`, `[[:space:]]*==[[:space:]]*` matches ` == `, and the regex then requires a literal `"` — but the source has `[`. No match. The other two alternatives (`add_argument("--self-test"` and `"--self-test" in sys.argv`) do not appear either; line 90's usage string is inside a plain `SystemExit(...)`, not a sys.argv comparison.

So the file is skipped by `continue` at line 1043 and never lands in `suite`. The enrolled-entry loop at worker-live.sh:1053-1057 then takes its refusal arm, prints `enrolled suite script yaml_dependency.py is missing or lost its self-test entrypoint`, and returns 1.

Blast radius: pr-gate.yml:290 runs `suite=$(bash scripts/worker-live.sh print-selftest-suite ...)` inside a `set -euo pipefail` step, so the required `gate` check's suite step aborts before any row runs. `registry_selftest_gate` calls the same derivation and dies identically. Net effect: the required gate is red, and the new helper's self-test — the only validation of `require_yaml`'s fail-closed behaviour — never executes in any lane.

Every already-enrolled script uses a recognised spelling (e.g. worker-issue.py:3110 `sys.argv[1] == "--self-test"`, gh_403.py:293 `"--self-test" in sys.argv[1:]`, ci-latency-alert.py:3067 `add_argument("--self-test"`), which is why this is the first entry to trip the check.
issues.title: Entrypoint spelling is invisible to the suite-enrollment discovery regex, so print-selftest-suite refuses and pr-gate's whole suite step dies

issues.body:
`_load_workflow_yaml(require)` is exercised only with an injected `refuse` callable, which means the `require is None` branch — the one that actually executes `from yaml_dependency import require_yaml` — is never covered by the two new rows at ci-latency-alert.py:1506-1510.

Consider the mutant that deletes the two lines inside `if require is None:` while leaving the branch. `require` stays None, `require("ci-latency workflow-seam checks")` raises `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not callable`, and TypeError is NOT in the `except (ImportError, RuntimeError)` tuple — so it escapes the module-level call at line 108 and the script dies at import with an unhandled TypeError rather than taking the structured detector path. Both new assertions stay green, because they never take that branch.

This is not a fail-open (the script dies loudly, and the two consumers at lines 477 and 1088 still raise AlarmError when `yaml is None`), so it is a test-coverage gap rather than a correctness defect — hence minor, not blocking.
issues.fix_hint:
Add one row that drives the real default path, e.g. temporarily shadow the helper so the genuine import fails and assert the structured tuple comes back:

  import sys as _sys
  _saved = _sys.modules.pop("yaml_dependency", None)
  _sys.modules["yaml_dependency"] = None  # forces ImportError on `from ... import`
  try:
      default_path = _load_workflow_yaml()
  finally:
      _sys.modules.pop("yaml_dependency", None)
      if _saved is not None:
          _sys.modules["yaml_dependency"] = _saved
  chk("yaml loader takes the structured path when the helper module itself cannot be imported",
      default_path[0] is None and isinstance(default_path[1], ImportError))

Alternatively, widen the except tuple to include TypeError so a deleted import cannot escape as an unhandled crash.
issues.title: The new loader self-test injects past the `from yaml_dependency import` line, so deleting that import is not caught

issues.body: `sys` is already imported at module scope (yaml_dependency.py:9) and used by `self_test()`. The `import sys` at line 87 inside `if __name__ == "__main__":` is a no-op rebinding of the same global name. Harmless, but it reads as if the module-level import were absent and invites a future reader to remove the wrong one.
issues.fix_hint: Delete line 87 (`import sys`) from the `__main__` block; the module-level import at line 9 already covers both `self_test()` and the CLI arm.
issues.title: Redundant `import sys` inside the `__main__` block shadows the module-level import

verdict.summary:
The refactor itself is sound: `require_yaml` is genuinely fail-closed (only ModuleNotFoundError with exc.name == 'yaml' is converted; a broken nested package re-raises unchanged), every consumer's failure path still raises rather than skipping (ci-latency-alert's `yaml is None` sites raise AlarmError; select-and-claim's try/except reds via `check(..., False, True)`), and the sparse-checkout audit is complete — all 10 sparse-checkout blocks live in 5 workflows, every block containing a new consumer gained `scripts/yaml_dependency.py`, and the one block that omits it (dispatch.yml:1582) reads worker-pr.py via `ast` only, never imports it. Every other consumer runs under a full checkout. REQUIRED_FILES additions line up with the corresponding sparse-checkouts. The worker-live.sh ERE extension keeps helper-using scripts classified as PyYAML consumers, and the new preflight row is non-vacuous (drop the ERE alternative and it goes red). The new yaml_dependency self_test has four rows that each invert on a wrong answer.

BLOCKING, however: `yaml_dependency.py` is enrolled in scripts/selftest-suite.txt but spells its entrypoint `sys.argv[1:] == ["--self-test"]`, which none of the three alternatives in worker-live.sh's discovery regex (worker-live.sh:1043) match — the list-literal RHS defeats the `== *"--self-test"` branch. `_derive_full_selftest_suite` therefore never adds it to `suite`, hits the enrolled-but-not-advertised arm at worker-live.sh:1053-1057, prints "enrolled suite script yaml_dependency.py is missing or lost its self-test entrypoint" and returns 1. That aborts `print-selftest-suite` at pr-gate.yml:290 under `set -euo pipefail`, so the required gate's entire suite step dies before a single row runs — and the new script's own self-test never executes anywhere. This is a mechanical one-line fix, but it fails the gate closed as written.
